paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: believing everything you hear is not faith, and God never asked you to do it. The writer says, "Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God." (1 John 4:1) He gives the reason right there: "many false prophets have gone out into the world." That means a loving, careful baker checks the recipe before it goes in the oven.

So what is the test? It all comes down to Jesus. "Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God." (1 John 4:2) A voice can sound kind, sound smart, and even sound holy, and I have met plenty of cookies that looked perfect and tasted like cardboard. But if it won't confess Jesus, it is not from God (1 John 4:3), and that gives you one clear question to ask of every voice.

Now hear the good news, because I want you to leave this one standing tall. The writer tells his readers, "You, little children, are from God and have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." (1 John 4:4) You are not testing the spirits alone, and you are not testing them scared. The One in you is greater, and that is how you tell "the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception." (1 John 4:6)
